skill.name: writing-beats
skill.description: Build an article interactively from fixed markdown notes, one selected beat at a time, while introducing concepts before relying on them.
skill.summary: Turn raw notes into a coherent article through grounded, user-selected beats.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive because the skill asks for a user-selected save path without inspecting the system. No semantic security issues were found.

static_findings.snippet: If the user did not say where to save the article, ask once and remember the path.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 11 asks the user where to save the article. It does not enumerate files, inspect system details, or perform reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Build Articles One Grounded Beat at a Time
content.value_statement: Unstructured notes make it difficult to create a clear article without losing the reader. This skill builds a user-directed sequence that introduces concepts before using them.
actual_capabilities: Establishes which concepts the target audience already understands.
Proposes two or three distinct starting beats from supplied markdown notes.
Tracks introduced concepts and limits later beats to grounded ideas.
Offers reachable next beats after rereading the current article.
Appends only the selected beat and preserves user edits.
Supports rewriting an earlier beat without replacing unrelated content.
limitations: Requires a fixed markdown file containing the source material.
Does not research facts or add information beyond the supplied notes.
Needs user choices throughout the drafting process.
Produces one beat at a time rather than a complete article immediately.

use_cases.title: Shape Technical Notes
use_cases.description: Convert technical notes into an article that explains each concept before later sections depend on it.

use_cases.title: Develop a Thought-Leadership Draft
use_cases.description: Explore several narrative openings and choose the direction that best supports the intended argument.

use_cases.title: Refine Educational Content
use_cases.description: Sequence examples and explanations according to what learners already know and what each beat introduces.

prompt_templates.title: Start From Raw Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use {notes_file} as the raw material and save the article to {article_file}. My audience already understands {prerequisites}.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a guided article from prepared notes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Opening Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest three starting beats for {audience}. Label the concepts each beat requires and introduces. Do not write until I choose.

prompt_templates.title: Continue From the Current Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Reread {article_file}. Offer three reachable next beats with different directions, and explain which concepts each option introduces.

prompt_templates.title: Revise the Article Path
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite beat {beat_number} using {new_direction}. Preserve other user edits, update the grounded concepts, and propose the next reachable beats.
prompt_templates.scenario: Change an earlier beat while maintaining article continuity.

output_examples.input: The notes cover cache benefits and invalidation. The audience understands HTTP but has not used application caches.
output: Option 1: Begin with a slow repeated request. Requires HTTP. Introduces repeated database work and caching.
Option 2: Begin with stale data after an update. Requires HTTP. Introduces cached responses and invalidation.

output_examples.input: Continue an article that already explains deployment frequency and small releases.
output: Option 1: Connect small releases to shorter feedback cycles. Introduces feedback latency.
Option 2: Show how smaller changes simplify incident diagnosis. Introduces change scope.

best_practices: Define audience prerequisites before selecting the first beat.
Choose beats that introduce only the concepts needed for later sections.
Review the article after each beat and preserve any user edits.
anti_patterns: Do not add unsupported claims that are absent from the source notes.
Do not rely on a concept before a prerequisite or earlier beat introduces it.
Do not draft several beats ahead of the user's selection.

faq.question: What source material does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a markdown file containing the raw notes, examples, arguments, or fragments for the article.

faq.question: Does it write the entire article at once?
faq.answer: No. It writes one selected beat, rereads the article, and then offers the next choices.

faq.question: What does grounding a concept mean?
faq.answer: A concept is grounded when the audience already knows it or an earlier beat clearly introduces it.

faq.question: Can it preserve my manual edits?
faq.answer: Yes. It rereads the article before writing and instructs the assistant to preserve user changes.

faq.question: Can I revise an earlier beat?
faq.answer: Yes. You can request a rewrite or a different direction for a specific beat.

faq.question: Does every note need to appear in the article?
faq.answer: No. The article ends when its journey is complete, even when some source fragments remain unused.
